key_insight: Boron nitride nanotubes host multiple room-temperature single-photon emitters at different visible wavelengths within one compact structure.
engineering_relevance: Their approximately 25 nm radius and multiwavelength emission could enable deterministic placement and integration into quantum-photonic waveguides and filters.
method: Locate and characterize emitters using confocal photoluminescence microscopy.
Assess single-photon emission using Hanbury Brown–Twiss interferometry.
Apply surface passivation or coating to mitigate blinking.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports emitters spanning the visible spectrum, lifetimes as short as 0.5 ns—about twice as fast as the fastest hBN emitters—and improved stability after surface treatment.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify photon purity, brightness, or device-integration performance, leaving practical source readiness uncertain.
paper_title: Room-Temperature Quantum Emission from Boron Nitride Nanotubes
